questions.note: Height, head and shoulder width sit close to the drawn man, but the arms read as thick uniform tubes from deltoid to wrist, and the trousers are skin-tight at the hip and crotch and baggy below. The proportions come across as a base mesh in a suit, not a man in kit.

Stance, lean, arm positions and the carbine's diagonal follow the reference in the onion overlay. Two things break the outline: the soldier's right boot is a low, shrink-wrapped shoe, and the pauldrons are flat cards that stick out where the reference shows rounded shells.

Every listed item is present and roughly where the drawing puts it. But the carrier front is a bare slab, the mag pouches are open boxes, the pauldrons are flat cards and the forearm guards are telescoping cylinders. The items are in the right places but read as placeholders, not believable real kit.

Several pieces float. The pauldron cards stand off the deltoid, small chips and clips hover off the elbow and arm bands, and the right knee pad gapes at its top edge. In the side and 3/4 views the radio pouch and a rear belt bracket stand clear of the body. I saw no clear interpenetration.

The upper body is bulky enough, but the carrier is a thin flat plate with none of the reference's loaded depth. The trousers cling like leggings at the seat and crotch. The kneepads and forearm guards have the right volume but read as hollow shells.

The right hand sits on the grip with the index finger along the receiver, and the support hand is under the handguard, so the hold is plausible. But the gloves are smooth glossy mannequin hands, and the stock floats in a thin wire triangle in front of the body instead of being tucked against it. The muzzle device is bare copper.

defects.what: The soldier's right boot vamp is a smooth shrink-wrapped shell with a hard horizontal seam at the collar, no toe cap, no rand and no laces below the ankle. It reads as a rubber galosh and does not match the laced left boot.
defects.fix: Build both boots from the same laced Zephyr-class upper: laces from the toe box up, a separate toe cap and mudguard rand, and panel seams on the vamp.

defects.what: The hair is a solid painted cap with a razor-hard edge across the forehead and temples, plus a few shard-like spikes on the crown. It has no strands, no hairline falloff and no fade at the sides.
defects.fix: Use groomed strands or cards with a soft, irregular hairline and short faded sides, with the longer textured top the reference shows.

defects.what: The wear is one procedural speckle mask at a single frequency and density. It is sprinkled evenly over the pauldrons, arm bands, forearm guards and knee pads as orange-tan flecks, with no concentration on edges or contact points.
defects.fix: Concentrate wear on edges, corners and high points as abrasion and scuffed paint, with dust in the recesses, and vary the scale from part to part.

defects.what: The trouser camo and dirt texture is low in texel density. Square pixel blocks and blurred blotches show on the shins, and the weave is visible in places but not in others.
defects.fix: Raise the texel density or use a tiling fabric base with a separate macro dirt mask, so the weave and pattern stay crisp at the knee and shin views.

defects.what: The trouser stacking above the boots is a set of evenly spaced, near-parallel horizontal ripples, like a sine displacement or accordion rings. It does not read as cloth bunching.
defects.fix: Real stacking is irregular: diagonal folds that collapse on the boot top, with one or two deep folds and the hem caught on the laces.

defects.what: The pauldron plates are flat, constant-thickness cards that stand off the deltoid, with a dark gap along their upper edges. They have no curvature to follow the shoulder and no strap to hold them.
defects.fix: Make them curved moulded shells that follow the deltoid, with rolled or bevelled edges and visible straps or hook-and-loop holding them to the sleeve.

defects.what: Two small square chips hover off the outside of the left elbow, unattached to any pad or strap.
defects.fix: Either a real elbow pad with a strap, or remove them.

defects.what: Bright silver buckle or clip blocks stick out from the upper-arm bands on both arms. They are untextured and float clear of the strap they belong to; the right arm's is at about [730,305,770,350] in pair_arm_R_cycles.png.
defects.fix: Thread the strap through a dark polymer ladder-lock that lies flat on the band.

defects.what: The forearm guards are stacks of concentric cylinders that flare like telescoping tubes, with no shell shape, padding or straps. The construction reads as a mech limb, not a strapped guard.
defects.fix: A moulded shell over a padded sleeve, wider at the elbow, held by two straps with buckles, and with seams and edge binding.

defects.what: The gloves are smooth glossy rubber casts of bare hands, with no seams, knuckle protection, palm patches or wrist closure. The fingers are uniform, sausage-like and evenly spaced.
defects.fix: M-Pact-class gloves have panelled synthetic leather, TPR knuckle and finger guards, a padded palm, a hook-and-loop cuff and fabric creases at the joints.

defects.what: The carrier front is a flat felt-like slab with no PALS webbing, binding or placard detail. The mag pouches are open-topped boxes with flat tabs standing up, all with the same crisp CG box edges.
defects.fix: Add a PALS grid with stitched webbing rows, bound edges, and a front placard with flapped or bungee-retained pouches that sag with their magazines.

defects.what: The trousers are skin-tight at the crotch and seat, with the base-mesh bulge and buttock shape showing through. They are a bodysuit at the hip and turn baggy only below the knee; the back turnaround shows it too.
defects.fix: G3-class combat trousers have ease at the seat and crotch, a gusset and a waistband standing off the body, so the cloth bridges the hollows instead of shrink-wrapping them.

defects.what: The soldier's right knee pad is a curved scoop standing off the knee, with an open dark gap along its top edge. It reads as hollow and unattached rather than strapped over the knee.
defects.fix: The pad seats on the knee with the cap on the patella. Its top edge tucks into the trouser's knee pocket or is pulled tight by the strap.

defects.what: The muzzle device is bright bare copper or bronze and shines against the otherwise flat black carbine. The orange stripes on the receiver read as decals, not anodised accents.
defects.fix: A flash hider is black phosphate or nitride with edge wear to grey steel; keep accent colours to the parts the reference shows them on.

defects.what: Two thin rigid rods with ball ends hang straight down below the thigh mag pouches. They read as stray wires or antennas.
defects.fix: If these are pull tabs, make them soft cord or webbing loops that drape, or remove them.

defects.what: In the side and 3/4 views the radio pouch on the back stands clear of the carrier with a gap behind it. A rear belt bracket juts out from the belt like an unattached block.
defects.fix: Mount the radio pouch flat on the back panel's PALS, and seat the rear belt pouch on the belt with its weight pulling it against the body.

defects.what: The leg-rig strap keepers on the soldier's right thigh are empty rectangular frames floating on the trouser surface, with no strap running through them.
defects.fix: Run the elastic leg strap through the buckles and around the thigh, compressing the cloth slightly.

defects.what: The buttstock is a thin dark wire triangle hanging in the air between the right forearm and the carrier. Its butt plate touches neither arm nor body.
defects.fix: The real stock is solid-sided and, in a low ready like this, rests against the carrier or is clamped by the inner forearm.

ranked: Overall impression: obviously computer-made. Every hard part has the same crisp box edges and constant thickness, and every fabric is a smooth shrink-wrapped shell. It reads as a game blockout dressed in placeholder textures.
[D3] One procedural speckle mask covers every hard surface at the same scale and density. Real wear concentrates on edges, corners and contact points.
[D1] The soldier's right boot is a seamless galosh with a hard collar seam and no laces down the vamp, next to a properly laced left boot. At the feet the mismatch is the most obvious giveaway.
[D12] The trousers cling to the crotch and seat like a bodysuit, so the base-mesh anatomy shows through. Combat trousers have ease there and bridge the hollows.
[D6] The pauldrons are flat cards standing off the shoulders with dark gaps behind them. The reference shows curved, strapped shells.
[D9] The forearm guards are telescoping concentric cylinders, a mech-limb construction with no shell shape, padding or straps.

[D11] The carrier front is a plain felt slab with no PALS grid, binding or placard, and the mag pouches are open boxes with flat tabs. The reference's loaded, webbed carrier has depth and many small layered parts.
[D10] The gloves are glossy mannequin hands with no panels, knuckle guards or cuffs. Together with the smooth skin-tight sleeves, the hands and arms read as rubber.
[D2] The hair is a painted cap with a razor edge across the forehead and a few spikes on the crown, with no strands and no fade.
[D5] The trouser stacking above the boots is a regular ladder of parallel ripples. Real stacking is irregular and collapses onto the boot top.
[D4] The trouser camo is low-res, with blocky pixels and blurred blotches on the shins, while other surfaces are crisp. The detail is sharp in one place and soft in the next.
[D13] The right knee pad gapes at the top like an empty scoop and does not sit on the knee.
[D16] The radio pouch and a rear belt bracket stand off the body in the side views. Nothing seems to be carrying their weight.
[D14] The bare copper muzzle device and orange decal stripes shine against an otherwise flat black, toy-like carbine.
All materials share one mid-roughness sheen: carrier, sleeves, trousers, gloves and pauldrons respond to the key the same way. The cordura, softshell, polymer and leather never separate.

Relative to the frame, the pauldrons and forearm guards are warm brown with tan flecks. The reference shows blue-grey painted steel with heavy grey wear, so the armour does not read as a different material from the cloth.
[D18] The stock is a thin wire triangle floating between forearm and carrier, so the low-ready hold looks posed rather than braced.
[D7] [D8] Small chips and bright silver clips hover off the elbows and arm bands, attached to nothing.
[D15] [D17] Rigid rods dangle under the thigh mag pouches, and the leg-rig keepers are empty frames with no strap through them.
Outside the scope, but it hurts the leg views: the plain floor's far edge cuts a hard horizon behind the thighs and knees. It makes the legs harder to read against the background.
